model.name: WebKit-reliable interactive elements: no fragile non-native tap targets (correct-by-construction, NEXT)
model.description: ★ NEXT / NOT-NOW (the FIX is a substantial SWEEP = needs a fresh expert, not the ~80% one; the sweep-DESIGN can start now; PO schedules the build). CORRECT-BY-CONSTRUCTION generalization of a recurring class: real iOS Safari/WebKit does NOT reliably fire tap/click on FRAGILE NON-NATIVE interactive elements (a div / span / h2 / implicit-label wired as a click target) that Chromium (incl. Playwright device EMULATION) DOES - so the headless gate goes GREEN while the real device FAILS = a FALSE-GREEN device-QA cycle. This hit >=3x: (1) R31.12 room-title h2 (->real button); (2) R31.12 config RADIO buttons (don't select on real iOS tap); (3) R30.53 Monaco codicon chevrons. RULE: EVERY interactive element MUST be a real button / real input (type=radio/checkbox/etc.) / [role=button]+tabindex with a WebKit-RELIABLE tap (native control, or pointerup/touchend + change - NOT a bare click on a non-native element). PLUS a STANDING LINT/SWEEP so a NEW fragile tap-target is caught BY CONSTRUCTION (at commit/CI), NOT by a Tron device-QA cycle. Together = the iOS-WebKit-tap-fire false-green is designed OUT, not chased one-at-a-time. Route (when scheduled): architect designs the sweep + lint rule, fresh expert implements the sweep, tester gates (lint fires on an injected fragile tap-target; sampled real controls fire on real @390 WebKit). Chain wires onto the built fix. Team-discovery (req-eng recurring-pattern flag, PO-approved 2026-07-27).

discoverySource.note: 3rd iOS-WebKit-tap-fire false-green in one sprint (h2-title, config radios; + R30.53 codicon) -> generalize to a correct-by-construction rule + standing lint so the class is designed out, not caught by a device-QA cycle each time. Marked NEXT (substantial sweep, fresh expert). See the memory 'ios-webkit-tap-fire-fragile-elements'.

model.crossRefNote: Generalizes the 3 instances: R31.12 (ede037dc) title-h2->real-button + config radios don't-select-on-iOS-tap; R30.53 Monaco codicon chevrons (render/interact only on real WebKit). Each was a false-green (Chromium/emulation passed, real iOS WebKit failed) caught by a Tron device-QA cycle. R31.15 designs the whole CLASS out by construction (native controls + standing lint).

acceptanceCriteria.text: NO interactive element is a fragile non-native tap target: NO div / span / h2 / implicit-label wired as a click/tap target. EVERY interactive element is a real <button>, a real <input> (radio/checkbox/text/etc.), or a [role=button]+tabindex=0 element - a proper accessible/native control.

Every interactive element FIRES/SELECTS reliably on a real iOS-WebKit tap - via a native control or pointerup/touchend + change, NOT a bare click handler on a non-native element (which Chromium fires but real WebKit does not). Sampled real controls fire on real @390 WebKit.

A STANDING LINT / SWEEP catches a NEW fragile tap-target BY CONSTRUCTION - at commit/CI, a click/tap handler bound to a non-native element (div/span/h2/implicit-label) FAILS the check. The class is caught by the lint, NOT by a Tron device-QA cycle. Testable: inject a fragile tap-target -> lint fires.

Captured scenario-first but marked NEXT / NOT-NOW: the FIX sweep is substantial (fresh expert, not the ~80% one); the sweep-DESIGN can start now. NOT dispatched for build until PO schedules; the chain (UC->Class->Method->Impl->Test) mints onto the built fix then.
